topic: Salman Shah's mother names new suspects in death case
headline_marked: Salman Shah's mother [[calls for questioning of Dipjol, Dolly Zahur]] in murder case
headline: Salman Shah's mother calls for questioning of Dipjol, Dolly Zahur in murder case
summary: Nila Chowdhury, mother of the late actor Salman Shah, has publicly named prominent film personalities, including Dipjol and Dolly Zahur, suggesting they hold crucial information or could be implicated in the long-running murder investigation.
details: Nila Chowdhury, mother of the late actor Salman Shah, has publicly called for the questioning of prominent film personalities Dipjol, Dolly Zahur, and Shiba Shanu in connection with her son's murder case. She believes they possess vital information regarding the circumstances of his death.

Her statements follow the recent arrest of actor Ashraful Haque alias Don, an accused in the Salman Shah murder case, at Shahjalal International Airport on August 10. Dipjol reportedly assisted in Don's apprehension, leading Chowdhury to suggest he be called as a witness.

Chowdhury stated that Dipjol, being active in the film industry during the time of Salman Shah's death, likely knows many events surrounding the incident. She believes his knowledge, good or bad, could aid the investigation and that he should testify as a witness.

She further alleged that Dolly Zahur knew much about the incident on the day Salman Shah was killed and has spoken about it in the media. Chowdhury suggested Dolly Zahur should be interrogated to ascertain her connection with Salman Shah's former wife, Samira, and could potentially be named as an accused.

Chowdhury also questioned how Don, an accused in a murder case, was able to cast his vote in the recent Film Artistes' Association election. She accused Shiba Shanu and others of welcoming Don, implying they provided him shelter instead of handing him over to the police.

Following Don's arrest, Salman Shah's uncle, Kumkum, has reportedly received renewed threats, which Nila Chowdhury says have been ongoing for a long time. She also claims Salman Shah's fans, who are demanding justice, are being threatened.

Salman Shah fan groups recently organized a human chain, demanding Don be taken on remand for interrogation and for the swift arrest and punishment of other accused, including Samira Haque. They threaten further protests in 64 districts if justice is delayed.

The murder case, filed last year, nearly 29 years after Salman Shah's death, names 11 individuals as accused. These include his former wife Samira Haque, actor Don Haque, Samira's mother Latifa Haque Lucy, businessman Aziz Mohammad Bhai, and others.

topic: Mirza Fakhrul sworn in as President, receives congratulations
headline_marked: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir [[elected as 23rd President of Bangladesh]]
headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected as 23rd President of Bangladesh
summary: The newly elected President will take his oath of office this evening at Bangabhaban after paying respects at the graves of Ziaur Rahman and Khaleda Zia.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. He secured 255 votes out of 349 in a parliamentary vote held on Thursday, August 20.

Following his election, the President-elect will visit Zia Uddyan in Dhaka on Friday, August 21, after the Jummah prayer to pay respects at the graves of martyred President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia.
The visit will include offering prayers and reciting Fateha at the tombs of the leaders.
The official swearing-in ceremony is scheduled to take place this evening at Bangabhaban, where he will formally assume the office of the President.
France and Switzerland have already extended their congratulations to the newly elected President.
caption:
255 votes out of 349: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is the new President of Bangladesh.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. He secured 255 votes out of 349 in a parliamentary vote held on Thursday, August 20.

Following his election, the President-elect will visit Zia Uddyan in Dhaka on Friday, August 21, after the Jummah prayer to pay respects at the graves of martyred President Ziaur Rahman and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia.

The visit will include offering prayers and reciting Fateha at the tombs of the leaders.

The official swearing-in ceremony is scheduled to take place this evening at Bangabhaban, where he will formally assume the office of the President.

France and Switzerland have already extended their congratulations to the newly elected President.
